title: Sales Enablement: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Deck, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Maya Robinson
body:
Summary:
Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that helps engineering teams ship LLM-powered features with predictable latency, lower unit costs, and enterprise-grade controls across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. This sales kit consolidates positioning and messaging, competitive briefings, a recommended pitch-deck outline, pricing guidance for typical motions, concise case studies, and a prospect-facing Security FAQ.

Use:
- Primary audience: AEs, Solutions Engineers, Sales Engineers, Customer Success, and GTM marketing.
- Purpose: Standardize messaging, enable rapid deal discovery, and reduce ramp time for technical customer conversations.

Target personas:
- ML/AI Platform Lead (SRE/Platform teams): cares about throughput, predictable latency, observability, and deployability to VPC/on-prem.
- ML Engineer / Model Owner: cares about model fidelity, quantization/optimization recommendations, and ease of model onboarding.
- Product/Engineering Manager: cares about time-to-market, cost per 1K tokens, availability and fallbacks.
- Security/Compliance Officer: cares about data residency, encryption, auditability, and contractual controls.

Positioning & messaging
- Positioning statement (short): "Redwood Inference: predictable, production-grade LLM inference that minimizes latency and unit cost — across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- Value props (short bullets):
  - Production economics: measurable unit-cost reductions via batching, caching, and optimized kernels.
  - Unified runtime: same API and tooling across hosted, reserved, and private modes.
  - Reliability-first: routing policies and fallbacks to keep applications online under load.
  - Enterprise controls: VPC/private control plane, KMS integrations, and audit logs.

One-liners / elevator pitches (pick by audience):
- For ML Platform: "Ship consistent LLM endpoints across environments — same API, predictable latency SLOs, and autoscaled reserved capacity when you need it."
- For Engineering/Product: "Cut inference costs and reduce latency with workload-aware batching, prefix caching, and fine-grained model variants — turn prototyping into production faster."
- For Security/Compliance: "Deploy Redwood Private with customer-managed VPC and KMS/HSM integrations plus audit logging and compliance evidence packages."

Proof points / data-driven bullets:
- Typical latency improvements observed in pilot customers: 20–55% median token latency reduction vs unoptimized baseline models.
- Cost savings from batching/caching and quantization recommendations: 30–70% per-token unit cost reduction depending on workload.
- Fleet reliability: 99.95% uptime SLA available on Dedicated.

Competitive brief (short summary + tactical talking points)
- Primary competitor categories:
  1. General cloud AI endpoint services (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI) — pro: deep cloud integrations; con: less workload-aware inference optimization and limited private deployment flexibility.
  2. LLM API providers (OpenAI, Anthropic) — pro: broad model catalog and rapid innovation; con: constrained deployment options and fewer enterprise private hosting controls.
  3. Inference/runtime vendors and self-hosted stacks (Replicate, OctoML, internal self-hosting) — pro: full control; con: heavy ops burden and inconsistent dev experience across teams.

- Competitive matrix (high-level):
Capability | Redwood Inference | OpenAI / Anthropic | AWS / Azure | Self-hosted stacks
---|---:|---:|---:|---:
Unified API across hosted/dedicated/private | Yes | No | Partial | No
Workload-aware batching & KV caching | Yes | No | Limited | Varies
Dedicated SLA-backed reserved capacity | Yes | No | Partial | Varies
Private VPC / on-prem package | Yes | No | Partial | Yes
Enterprise observability & cost breakdowns | Yes | Limited | Limited | Varies
Customer-managed KMS/HSM | Yes | No | Partial | Yes

Tactical talking points by competitor:
- Against cloud providers: emphasize latency/cost determinism and inference optimizations tailored to LLM workloads plus migration/fallback policies.
- Against LLM API vendors: emphasize deployment choices (dedicated/private), auditability, and price predictability for sustained production traffic.
- Against self-hosted approaches: emphasize time-to-value, managed optimizations, and fewer infra maintenance costs.

Objection handling (common)
- "Why not just use OpenAI/Azure?" — For early experiments, those are excellent; for production apps with predictable cost/latency and regulatory constraints, Redwood provides the deploy modes and economics tooling needed to scale safely.
- "We can self-host to save money." — Self-hosting can reduce sticker price but often increases TCO: engineering overhead, unpredictable tail latency, and slow ops cycles. Redwood reduces both ops and unit-cost via runtime optimizations and platform tooling.

Recommended pitch deck — slide-by-slide outline
1. Title / Hook — 1-liner + logo
2. Customer pain — concrete latency, cost, and reliability examples
3. Redwood thesis — serving is the competitive layer; inference economics matter
4. Product snapshot — hosted / dedicated / private modes (one-slide matrix)
5. How it works (Runtime + Smart routing + Caching & Batching) — 2–3 visuals
6. Performance benchmarks — latency, throughput, unit cost comparisons (customer or internal benchmarks)
7. Security & compliance — VPC, KMS, audit logs, SOC2/ISO roadmap
8. Pricing & capacity options — quick reference (see pricing guidance)
9. Case studies / reference customers — outcomes + metrics
10. Deployment & onboarding plan — pilot → dedicated → rollout
11. Ask / next steps — trial, POC checklist, contact

Pitch tips for SEs:
- Start with the customer’s SLOs (latency, throughput) and current pain (cost, outages) — tailor proof points.
- Use internal benchmark numbers only when customer workload aligns; prefer customer pilot data when possible.
- For security-sensitive customers, route to Private deployment early and involve Security SME.

Pricing guidance (playbook)
- Pricing pillars (talking approach):
  - Hosted: usage-based (per-token / per-embedding), best for early-stage and variable traffic.
  - Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity + overage; priced for predictable throughput and SLA commitments.
  - Private: platform licensing + support/ops fee; for regulated or air-gapped deployments.

- Example pricing bands (illustrative, adjust per deal):
Mode | Typical contract | Pricing drivers
Hosted (Self-serve) | Month-to-month | per-token; model family; inference tier (standard/optimized)
Dedicated (Reserved) | 6–36 month commit | committed GPU hours, peak concurrency, SLA level
Private (Enterprise) | Annual license | deployment complexity, on-prem packaging, integration, support tier

- Negotiation playbook:
  1. For SMB / POC: offer 30–90 day trial credits on Hosted and attach a lightweight POC SOW that includes sample workload and acceptance criteria.
  2. For mid-market: bundle Dedicated commits with onboarding credits and 3–6 month success milestones.
  3. For enterprise: map pricing to business KPIs (cost per query, latency SLOs, availability) — include professional services and extended support as separate line items.

- Discount levers (approved): contract length, committed spend, support tier, exclusivity for select models (rare).

Case studies (anonymized/representative)
1) Conversational commerce startup — Outcome: 45% reduction in median response latency; 52% reduction in inference cost per session.
  - Situation: migrating from multi-region OpenAI endpoints with unpredictable tail latency.
  - Action: Pilot on Redwood Hosted with prefix caching + model variant routing; moved to Dedicated reserved pool for peak shopping periods.
  - Metrics: median latency from 430ms → 240ms; per-session inference cost down 52% after batching and quantization recommendations; improved checkout conversions by 3.2%.

2) Financial data SaaS (regulated) — Outcome: Private deployment with customer-managed VPC and KMS, SOC2 evidence completed; predictable 99.95% uptime and 30% unit-cost improvement vs prior self-host.
  - Situation: needed on-prem data controls and audit trails for regulated customers.
  - Action: Deployed Redwood Private with on-prem package, integrated with customer’s HSM and SAML SSO; implemented model pinning and canary rollouts.
  - Metrics: SLA met at 99.95%; inference cost down 30% after autoscaling policies and KV caching; deployment completed in 10 weeks.

Security FAQ (for prospects)
Q: Where does customer data live? A: Hosted data is stored in regionally-selected cloud accounts with tenant isolation. For regulated workloads, we recommend Redwood Private where the customer controls the VPC and storage.

Q: How is data protected in transit and at rest? A: TLS 1.2+ for in-transit; AES-256 for data at rest. For Private deployments, customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported and required for highest-sensitivity workflows.

Q: Can we bring our own keys (BYOK)? A: Yes — Redwood supports KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM for Private deployments.

Q: Do you provide audit logs and access trails? A: Yes — requestable audit logs include request identifiers, user tokens, model version, time, and resource consumption. Logs can be routed to customer SIEM via syslog/S3/GCS connectors in Private/Dedicated modes.

Q: What compliance certifications do you have? A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II (in progress or roadmap depending on date). For enterprise customers, we provide compliance evidence packages and support ISO27001 assessment requests; contact Security for details.

Q: How is model privacy handled? A: We do not use customer-provided prompts or outputs to train public models. For Hosted mode, we offer a data handling agreement; for Dedicated/Private, data is isolated and can be configured to never leave customer-controlled infrastructure.

Q: What is the incident notification process? A: We provide SLA-backed incident notification for Dedicated customers, including dedicated pager rotations, status updates, and post-incident reports. See the Incident Response runbook for timelines and escalation paths.

Onboarding & POC checklist (technical)
1. Define target workload (QPS, median/99th latency SLOs, typical sequence lengths).
2. Choose deployment mode: Hosted trial → Dedicated reserved → Private (if required).
3. Provide representative prompt set + eval metrics (quality acceptance criteria).
4. Run pilot (2–6 weeks): collect token/latency/cost telemetry; review optimization recommendations.
5. Agree success criteria and scale plan; sign commit for Dedicated or license for Private.

Ownership & escalation
- GTM owner: AE / Solutions Engineering (primary contact for deal motion)
- Technical owner (pilot/onboarding): Solutions Engineering / Customer Success Engineering
- Security & compliance: Security team (contact: security@redwood.example)
- Legal & contracting: finance-and-legal (contact: contracts@redwood.example)

- Demo script (2–3 minute performance demo):

  2. Run a 1-minute burst at target QPS showing stable p99 latency.
  3. Show cost dashboard highlighting per-route cost breakdown.
